solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: John, for one, a powerless former president

indicators.note: less means without, so P, the physics symbol for power, is dropped from the word

parts.note: John the Baptist is one example of a baptist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps a man called John, described as a former head of state who has lost all power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' is not a name to use as letters: he is John the Baptist, so 'for one' gives BAPTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulgencio Batista ruled Cuba as president until Castro's revolution of 1959.

clue.text: Bond — finish off dodgy agent

parts.note: bail is money put up as a bond for release

indicators.note: finish off means the last letter is removed

parts.note: iffy is slang for dubious or dodgy

explanation.surface: A spy like James Bond is told to kill a double-dealing agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is a legal bond, bail.
explanation.definitionFit: A court officer who acts on behalf of a sheriff or landlord, seizing goods, is an agent of the law.

clue.text: Operation tails one having left estate

indicators.note: having left means the letter for one has gone from the word

parts.note: trains are the long tails of gowns
I is the Roman numeral for one
a plantation is a large agricultural estate

explanation.surface: An operation follows someone who has quit an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tails' reads as a verb, following, but it is a noun: trains are the trailing tails of dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery that moves an organ or tissue from donor to recipient is a type of surgical procedure.

clue.text: Second fish stabbed with hard stiletto

indicators.note: stabbed with means pierced, so the hard letter is driven into the fish

parts.note: the pike eel is a fish
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A second fish has been knifed with a sharp stiletto blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiletto' suggests a dagger, matching 'stabbed', but it is a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto in footwear is a high thin heel, the shoe style also called by the other name.

clue.text: Disengaged, to some extent, about girl

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters run backwards
to some extent means only part of the word is used

explanation.surface: A young woman who is partly disengaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' takes SENGA from inside Disengaged, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A feminine given name, so a girl in crossword terms, where any female name can stand for girl.

clue.text: Butts or tails?

definitions.meaning: the stubs left once cigarettes have been smoked
a dog's tail is literally the end of the dog, hence the query

explanation.surface: A question about cigarette stubs or the hind parts of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: splitting the phrase gives the ends of dogs, which is what tails are.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-ends is informal British slang for cigarette stubs; tails are literally the hind ends of dogs.

clue.text: Simple performances, not duties made complex

indicators.note: made complex means jumbled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Easy shows without any obligations get complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Short, simple pieces for two voices or players, the diminutive of the Italian for a duet.

clue.text: Stick with barrel of Irish stew

parts.note: gum is glue, something that sticks
the O' in Irish surnames such as O'Grady means of, descended from

explanation.surface: Glue together with a cask of Irish stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The O' in Irish surnames is read as 'of', so 'of Irish' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick soup or stew from Louisiana, thickened with okra.

clue.text: Study nervous matter when astride potty

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so one word sits across the other

parts.note: neurology is the subject concerned with the nervous system
psycho is slang for mad or potty

explanation.surface: A nervous child is seen doing schoolwork while sitting on a potty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' hints at toilet training; it is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch of science linking brain function with behaviour and thought is a field of study.

clue.text: In a way, schoolgirl's quick in Germany

indicators.note: in a way says each half of schoolgirl is to be given in some form, so the plain word girl gives way to a particular girl, Nell

parts.note: schoolgirl is read as two words, with school given its usual abbreviation SCH and girl kept for now

explanation.surface: In some way, a German schoolgirl is fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' tells the solver to split schoolgirl into school and girl, then render each: SCH for school, and NELL as an example of a girl. The blog reads it the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for fast or rapid, familiar from the shouted command to hurry up.

clue.text: It expanded into hate mail with virtue — oddly perverse

indicators.note: perverse means twisted or contrary, so the gathered letters are rearranged
oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Something grew into a stream of abusive letters accompanied by a strangely twisted virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a mere pronoun, but in the British drink order 'gin and it' it is short for the vermouth; 'expanded' asks for the full name.
explanation.definitionFit: In bar shorthand, especially the British gin and it, 'it' abbreviates the sweet red vermouth from Italy.

clue.text: Profits from paper when leader is cut

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is cut away from the word for paper

parts.note: tissue is a thin soft paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's earnings when its editor-in-chief is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profits' is fair: one dictionary sense of the answer is the yield or profits arising from land or other property. 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal and dictionary usage the word means the yield or proceeds produced by land or property.

clue.text: Drunken old coves keeping too much aside

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other
drunken means reeling and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: Tipsy old blokes are hanging on to more than they should, set off to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges O and COVES into SOVOCE; 'keeping' puts the other piece after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian musical and theatrical term for speaking in an undertone, much as an actor's private remark is made.

clue.text: It will disappoint very little wife in large chair

parts.note: sweet FA is slang for nothing at all
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: in places the wife letter inside the chair word

parts.note: a sedan is a sedan chair, a carried enclosed seat

explanation.surface: A tiny wife sitting in an oversized chair is bound to be a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: FA comes from the British slang 'sweet FA', meaning nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief glow in the sky before sunrise raises hopes of morning that are then dashed, so figuratively any promise that disappoints.

clue.text: Whereon plucky action occurs in one's mind

definitions.text: Whereon plucky action occurs in one's mind

parts.words: Whereon plucky action occurs in one's mind
parts.note: plucky reads as brave but means plucked like strings: an imaginary instrument mimed by a rock fan

explanation.walkthrough: 'plucky' looks like courage but means plucking strings, done on an instrument that exists only in the imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: Miming rock guitar playing with no real instrument, the strumming exists only in the imagination.

clue.text: Fibre glass one broke — that's no good

indicators.note: broke means shattered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
that's no tells us the good letter is removed from the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone broke a glass made of fibre, and the result is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: LASS, which is glass without its G, joins I before 'broke' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong plant fibre from an agave, used for rope, twine and matting.

clue.text: More certain to secure split yield

indicators.note: to secure means to hold within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: surer means more certain
rend means to tear or split

explanation.surface: Being more confident about holding fast to a split harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yield' suggests a harvest, but here it is the verb to give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give up or give in, conceding defeat to an opponent.

clue.text: Tired bishop's obstinate and obsessive

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
anal, short for anally retentive, describes someone fussily obsessive and stubborn

explanation.surface: A weary clergyman who is stubborn and fixated on detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired in the sense of hackneyed or stale, as with a worn-out joke, means commonplace and dull.

clue.text: Ask for brief pointer about god!

parts.note: to beg is to ask for

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters run backwards
brief means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an arrow points the way

explanation.surface: Requesting a short signpost about a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims ARROW to ARRO, and 'about' turns it to ORRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish exclamation, a mild oath derived from saying by God.

clue.text: Southern critters chewed hampers

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Little creatures in the South have gnawed through the picnic baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampers' poses as baskets the critters chewed, but it is a verb meaning hinders.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper someone is to hinder or limit their movement, so both verbs mean confine or impede.

clue.text: Small offensive boy in hat

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the Tet Offensive was a 1968 attack in the Vietnam War
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A rude little lad wearing a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective, rude, but it is a noun naming a military attack. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed, high-crowned cowboy hat named after its American maker.

clue.text: Ligature getting caught damaged part of sight

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A tied ligature snagged and harmed part of someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sight' is not vision but a gunsight or telescope sight. 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A network of fine crosshairs or a grid in the eyepiece of a telescope or gun sight.

clue.text: Restless and malicious, blowing cover

indicators.note: blowing cover means losing the outer layer, here the first letter

parts.note: bitchy means spiteful or malicious

explanation.surface: Someone fidgety and spiteful whose disguise has been exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fidgety and impatient to move, as with itchy feet, is being unable to stay still.

clue.text: Regularly serve Audrey's duck

indicators.note: regularly picks every second letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Audrey keeps serving duck at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' suggests a bird on the menu, but it is the verb to dodge. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or avoid it, as a question or a blow.

clue.text: Call up first lady to accept fine

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Telephone the president's wife to get her to agree to pay a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a president's wife; here it is Eve, the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon or bring a memory or feeling to mind, as a scent can conjure up a place.

clue.text: Pets commonly on lead caught in sheet

indicators.note: on means placed upon, so the sounded word comes first, ahead of the pets
caught in the sense of heard tells us the word for lead is judged by its sound

parts.note: a rein is a strap for leading or guiding a horse
the two most common household pets are named together

explanation.surface: Household animals out on a lead get trapped under a bedsheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheet' is a verb here, for rain falling in sheets, not a bed sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: When it sheets down, rain falls in heavy torrents, the same as the idiom for a downpour.

clue.text: One teasing old queen, perhaps, about obesity in a heartless manner

indicators.note: about means around, so the queen's letters go round the others

parts.note: Anne Regina is one example of a past queen, Anne plus R for Regina

indicators.note: heartless removes all the middle of the word, leaving just its two outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone mocking a former monarch about her weight in an unkind way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' is not unkindness but the loss of every inner letter of obesity, leaving OY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who teases is an irritant who gets under people's skin, hence a pest who irritates.

clue.text: After not much time, noble French city joined by commoner?

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman

indicators.note: commoner is read as a common letter: the two words overlap on a shared letter, so it is written only once

parts.note: Lyon is a large city in France

explanation.surface: Shortly afterwards, a nobleman of a French city was joined by an ordinary man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commoner' suggests a non-noble; it means the letter common to both words, the L they share.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something happening at an initial stage, soon after a start, before much time has gone by.
